summary: WebSocket-driven PTY, arbitrary file I/O, and remote self-upgrade on the installer's host
details: On startup the package connects to a WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, configurable) and processes peer-supplied control frames. A `terminal_input` handler writes attacker-supplied bytes directly into a spawned PTY (bash on Linux/macOS, PowerShell on Windows) running as the service user, giving the remote peer an interactive shell (handleTerminalInput → term.pty.write(msg.data)). A separate `upgrade_agent` handler shells out to `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest`, writes a detached upgrade script, and restarts the systemd/launchd/PM2 unit, letting the peer swap the running package on demand. The message router additionally dispatches `read_file`, `write_file`, `list_directory`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `transfer_files`, and git operations to workbench handlers, so the peer can read, write, move, or exfiltrate any file the agent process can access. Access is gated only by a shared `AGENT_SECRET`; possession of that secret grants full-host RCE and filesystem access. `service/linux.js` also prepends `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` to PATH in the installed systemd unit.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
